results: 1. trigger or provoking activity: action-induced and restricted to a few body segments, suggesting cortical-reflex myoclonus
2. medication and anaesthetic exposure: propofol and thiopentone for coronary artery bypass grafting with aortic valve replacement; jerks began 6 days later (day 3 in the second case)
3. interictal EEG: occasional OCCIPITAL SHARP WAVES only (normal in the second patient) - no ictal pattern
4. antiseizure medication trial: complete resolution within 4 days on clonazepam 0.25 mg twice daily and levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily, with no relapse on follow-up
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Delayed-onset postoperative cortical-reflex myoclonus induced by anesthetic exposure (propofol/thiopentone) after CABG with aortic valve replacement

ALTERNATIVE: Postoperative epileptic myoclonus

ALTERNATIVE: Hypoxic–ischemic myoclonus after cardiac surgery

ALTERNATIVE: Metabolic or medication-induced myoclonus
dx: Delayed-onset postoperative cortical-reflex myoclonus induced by anesthetic exposure (propofol/thiopentone) after CABG with aortic valve replacement
